extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, and PR/communications practitioners researching Burson and PR industry practices
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic company profile summarizing Burson (formerly Burson Cohn & Wolfe / Burson-Marsteller): history, services, practices, notable campaigns, and internal methodologies used in public relations and crisis management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation capital framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses a framework and consulting methodology to assess and actively manage what it refers to as 'reputation capital' across four areas: company actions, communications, social narratives, and stakeholder beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This framework is used to build and protect reputations; the page presents the four areas as the core dimensions for assessing reputation and guiding communications strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis management practice (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide communications with clients' employees, customers and the general public during crises; develop contingency plans; provide intelligence and market research; and provide communications tools and techniques intended to help companies recover following a crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burson established a global Issues & Crisis Group with certified experts, offers contingency planning, hourly/daily intelligence reports advising on issues and public reception, and market research into CEO and corporate reputation. The page cites numerous high-profile crisis cases (Tylenol, Three Mile Island, Bhopal) as exemplars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press conference and media engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize and conduct press conferences and proactive media engagement as a core crisis response tactic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Burson organized a press conference televised across 35 markets for the Tylenol crisis and facilitated daily press conferences and an information center during Bhopal; media briefings are shown as central to crisis communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product recall and safety-response communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Use product recalls, introduction of safety measures, and subsequent consumer-facing communications as components of crisis response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tylenol case: recommended nationwide recall, introduced tamper-proof (triple-sealed) packaging, reintroduced product with ads and coupons to rebuild consumer trust — presented as a model response that led to sales recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency planning and preparedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist clients in developing contingency plans for potential crises and prepare response protocols in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burson's Issues & Crisis Group and training programs are described as providing contingency-planning services and certified expertise to prepare clients for crises before they occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligence reporting and issue monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clients with intelligence reports (hourly or daily) advising of new issues, public reception, and critical or supportive responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These monitoring reports are used during crises to inform decision-making and adaptation of communications tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-Based Communications / DIGS
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a scientific, data-driven approach to communications: 'DIGS' (digital, integrated, global, strategic) and 'Evidence-Based Communications'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduced under Mark Penn's leadership as an organizational strategy drawing on research; positioned as integrating data/science into communications planning and execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and institutionalizing practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing employee training to create a uniform approach to public relations across clients and locations, tailored to be culturally appropriate; includes formal programs such as Burson-Marsteller University.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is described as a core part of the firm's operation (historically ~65% of costs related to human resources), with specialized training for practice areas (e.g., Issues & Crisis Group) and a global executive training university.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate PR practice specialties
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate and financial communications practice focusing on corporate brand positioning, financial communications, organizational performance, and C-suite positioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four specialties are listed as the focus areas for the firm's corporate PR work, demonstrated via long-term corporate client relationships and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Healthcare communications practice standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations and communications for pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare provider, policy, nutrition, cosmetics and consumer health markets; executing awareness campaigns and product/brand launches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Firm's healthcare practice was top-ranked by industry reports and has run campaigns like National Breast Cancer Awareness Month; awards and client lists are provided as evidence of capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large-scale promotional events and experiential PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan and execute large promotional events that combine entertainment/sports to generate publicity and public engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: organizing the AT&T Olympic Torch Relay and conceiving Hands Across America; described as requiring significant staffing and coordination to create high-profile media moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of third-party/grassroots advocacy (and associated risks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize or support third-party groups and coalitions to influence public opinion or policymakers (e.g., creating or supporting advocacy groups to target legislators or consumers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page documents the National Smokers Alliance and other industry-funded groups organized during tobacco-related campaigns; guidance is implicit via documented controversy and criticism about concealment of sponsor funding and ethical concerns (an anti-pattern).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggressive media-placement / 'whisper' campaign tactics (and reputational risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitching or placing negative commentary about competitors via influencers or former journalists as a tactical media approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described via the Google smear campaign: soliciting negative articles and using former reporters to push critical coverage led to public backlash and the firm parting ways with the client — presented as a risky tactic with reputational consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical client engagement limits (tobacco policy example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt policies restricting work for certain industries on ethical grounds (example: Burson-Marsteller committed in 2010 to no longer accept work on behalf of the tobacco industry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites this policy change as an organizational ethical stance and a change in client-acceptance practice.
